title: Log in
kind: a build chapter: the windows every player sees before the map
one: You turn frmLogin into the Log in window. It checks the username and password, locks for 30 seconds after 3 wrong tries, and opens the Register window from chapter 5.

stages.title: See what the Log in window does

screens.title: Look at the Log in window and what it checks

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, you will know what happens when a player clicks **Log in**.
Summit Ready starts on the Log in window. A player types their username and password, then clicks **Log in**.

screenshot.alt: The Log in window, with the Mourne banner along the top and the log in box under the title
screenshot.cap: The Log in window that you build in this chapter.

blocks.p: The rules for logging in are numbered 12 to 15, and the notes in the code use those numbers. Rules 12 and 13: if the username box or the password box is blank, a red message says which box to fill in. Rule 14: if the username and password do not match a player in `players.txt`, a red message says so.
Rule 15: after 3 wrong tries in a row, the **Log in** button stops working for 30 seconds, and counts down each second. That slows down anyone who tries to guess a password.
When the username and password match, the Log in window hides and the Welcome window opens. The Welcome window is empty for now. Chapter 7 fills it.
**Register a new player** opens the Register window from chapter 5. After a player registers, their new username is already typed in the Username box.

screens.title: Check that your project is ready, and see the words this chapter uses

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, you will know that your project has everything the Log in window needs.

need: You need frmLogin with its menu bar, File and Help (chapter 2).
The file `banner.jpg`, one of the 3 pictures in the Images folder inside bin\Debug (chapter 2).
The two error types BlankFieldException and LoginFailedException, which you made earlier (chapter 4).
The Register window, frmRegister, which holds the new player's username in `NewUsername` (chapter 5).
About 2 hours. Your ticks are kept, so you can stop at the end of any screen and come back later.

words: and
`&&` means and. The `if` is true only when both of its parts are true.
timer
A control that runs a method again and again, after the same wait each time. You cannot see a timer on the window when the program runs.
Interval
The wait of a timer between one tick and the next, in thousandths of a second. 1000 is one second.
Tick
The event a timer has each time its Interval runs out.
Enabled
A control with Enabled set to false is grey, and clicking it does nothing.
LinkLabel
A label whose words work like a link on a web page.
ShowDialog
Opens a window and waits. The next line runs only after that window closes.
Hide
`this.Hide()` hides the window without closing it. `this.Show()` brings it back.
Focus
`txtPassword.Focus()` puts the flashing cursor in the Password box, ready to type.
ToLower
Gives the same text with every capital letter made small, so `Bog` and `bog` compare as equal.
blocks.intro: You do not need to learn these words now. Where you first meet each one in the chapter, it has a dotted line under it. Hover over it or tap it to see what it means.

screens.title: Add LogIn to the PlayerFile class

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, PlayerFile can find the player with a username and password.
LogIn checks for blank boxes first. If both boxes are blank, the message asks for both. Then it looks through every player in `players.txt` for one that matches.
The username matches with or without capital letters, so `Bogtrotter` finds bogTrotter. The password must match exactly.

code.title: PlayerFile.LogIn
partLines: LogIn is given the 2 boxes, and gives back a Player.
`blank` collects a message for each blank box. If it is not empty, LogIn throws a BlankFieldException with that message. `Trim` ignores spaces, so a username of spaces counts as blank.
`LoadAll` from chapter 3 reads every player. [[ToLower|9]] makes both usernames small letters, so capitals do not matter. The first player that matches is given back.
If no player matches, LogIn throws a LoginFailedException.

screens.title: Finish btnLogIn_Click, which counts the wrong tries

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, a wrong log in shows a message, and the third wrong try in a row starts the wait.

A wrong username or password throws a LoginFailedException. A blank box throws a BlankFieldException, a kind of SummitException. C# uses the first `catch` that fits, so the LoginFailedException `catch` goes first.
A blank box is not counted as a wrong try.

code.title: btnLogIn_Click: a wrong log in
partLines: `wrongTries++` adds one to the count. The password box is emptied, and [[Focus|8]] puts the cursor in it.
On the third wrong try in a row, StartWait begins the 30 seconds. Otherwise the message shows.
The message says which box to fill in.

screens.title: Your turn: make the wait 10 seconds

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, you have changed the length of the wait, and tested it, on your own.
30 seconds is a long wait when you are testing. Change the wait to 10 seconds, test it, then change it back.

code.title: Make the wait 10 seconds
task: In StartWait, change 30 to 10 in the red message that says **Three wrong tries. Wait 30 seconds, then try again.**
code.test: Press F5. Type `summitSeeker` and a wrong password, then click Log in. Do this 3 times in a row.
code.expect: The button says **Try again in 10 seconds** and counts down to Log in.
code.hint: StartWait has 2 places with 30 in them. The line at the top of frmLogin that sets the wait stays as it is.

blocks.p: When the test passes, change both back to 30, because the rule says 30 seconds.

glossary: and
`&&` means and. The `if` is true only when both of its parts are true.
timer
A control that runs a method again and again, after the same wait each time. You cannot see a timer on the window when the program runs.
Interval
The wait of a timer between one tick and the next, in thousandths of a second. 1000 is one second.
Tick
The event a timer has each time its Interval runs out.
Enabled
A control with Enabled set to false is grey, and clicking it does nothing.
LinkLabel
A label whose words work like a link on a web page.
ShowDialog
Opens a window and waits. The next line runs only after that window closes.
Hide
`this.Hide()` hides the window without closing it. `this.Show()` brings it back.
Focus
`txtPassword.Focus()` puts the flashing cursor in the Password box, ready to type.
ToLower
Gives the same text with every capital letter made small, so `Bog` and `bog` compare as equal.
